title: Build an AI-Powered Customer Analytics Dashboard
subtitle: Capstone Project — Apply all 5 modules in a real-world scenario
overview:
You are a data analyst at a mid-sized e-commerce company. The Head of Customer Success has asked you to build a comprehensive AI-powered analytics system that combines everything you've learned in this course.

Your system will: clean and prepare messy customer data using AI techniques, engineer predictive features, build a churn prediction model, analyze customer feedback with NLP, and present findings in a governance-compliant framework — all while documenting your approach for a non-technical executive audience.
objectives: Apply AI-assisted data cleaning to a realistic messy dataset
Engineer meaningful features using automated and domain-driven techniques
Build and evaluate a customer churn prediction model
Perform sentiment analysis on customer feedback text
Generate an executive summary using LLM-assisted report writing
Document bias checks and governance considerations
Present findings in a clear, stakeholder-ready format

steps.title: Data Exploration & Quality Assessment
steps.description: Load the dataset and perform a comprehensive quality assessment using automated profiling tools. Identify missing values, outliers, duplicates, and data type issues before writing a single line of cleaning code.
steps.dataGeneratorScript:
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
import random
import string

# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# SYNTHETIC DATASET GENERATOR — ecommerce_customers.csv
# Run this script FIRST to create your dataset.
# Produces 10,000 records with realistic quality issues:
#   • Missing values in income, age, job_title, last_purchase_date
#   • ~3% duplicate records (same customer, slightly different data)
#   • Outliers in account_balance and avg_order_value
#   • 200+ messy job_title variants (needs standardization)
#   • Churn labels correlated with behavioral signals
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

np.random.seed(42)
random.seed(42)
N = 10_000

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
def random_date(start, end):
    delta = end - start
    return start + timedelta(days=random.randint(0, delta.days))

def rand_str(n=8):
    return ''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=n))

# ── Demographics ─────────────────────────────────────────────
first_names = ["James","Mary","John","Patricia","Robert","Jennifer",
               "Michael","Linda","William","Barbara","David","Susan",
               "Richard","Jessica","Joseph","Sarah","Thomas","Karen",
               "Charles","Lisa","Christopher","Nancy","Daniel","Betty"]
last_names  = ["Smith","Johnson","Williams","Brown","Jones","Garcia",
               "Miller","Davis","Rodriguez","Martinez","Hernandez",
               "Lopez","Gonzalez","Wilson","Anderson","Thomas","Taylor"]

names = [f"{random.choice(first_names)} {random.choice(last_names)}" for _ in range(N)]
emails = [f"{n.lower().replace(' ','.')}.{rand_str(4)}@{'gmail.com' if random.random()<0.5 else 'yahoo.com'}"
          for n in names]

ages = np.random.normal(38, 12, N).clip(18, 80).astype(int)
incomes = np.random.lognormal(10.8, 0.6, N).clip(20_000, 300_000).round(-2)

regions = np.random.choice(
    ["Northeast","Southeast","Midwest","Southwest","West","Northwest"],
    N, p=[0.22,0.18,0.20,0.12,0.18,0.10]
)

# ── Messy job titles (200+ variants → 15 canonical categories) ──
canonical_jobs = {
    "Software Engineer":   ["Software Engineer","SWE","Software Dev","software engineer","SW Engineer","Sftwr Engr"],
    "Data Analyst":        ["Data Analyst","data analyst","Data Anlt","Analytics Analyst","Data Anaylst"],
    "Manager":             ["Manager","Mgr","manager","MANAGER","Manger","Mngr"],
    "Teacher":             ["Teacher","Educator","teacher","Tchr","Instructor","Prof"],
    "Nurse":               ["Nurse","RN","Registered Nurse","nurse","Nrs","Nursing"],
    "Sales Representative":["Sales Rep","Sales Representative","Sales","sales rep","Slsrep"],
    "Accountant":          ["Accountant","CPA","accountant","Acct","Accounting"],
    "Marketing Specialist":["Marketing Specialist","Marketing","Mktg Spec","Marketer","mktg"],
    "Engineer":            ["Engineer","Engr","engineer","ENGINEER","Engnr"],
    "Doctor":              ["Doctor","MD","Physician","Dr.","physician"],
    "Consultant":          ["Consultant","Cnslt","consultant","Consulting","Consult"],
    "Designer":            ["Designer","UX Designer","Graphic Designer","designer","Dsgn"],
    "Project Manager":     ["Project Manager","PM","Proj Mgr","project manager","ProjMgr"],
    "HR Specialist":       ["HR Specialist","Human Resources","HR","hr specialist","H.R."],
    "Other":               ["Other","N/A","NA","Self-employed","Retired","Student","Freelancer"],
}
all_variants = [v for variants in canonical_jobs.values() for v in variants]
job_titles = np.random.choice(all_variants, N)

# ── Dates ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
base_date = datetime(2020, 1, 1)
end_date  = datetime(2024, 6, 30)
signup_dates = [random_date(base_date, end_date) for _ in range(N)]

# ── Behavioral signals (correlated with churn) ────────────────
# Base churn probability driven by behavioral features
months_since_signup = np.array([(end_date - d).days / 30 for d in signup_dates])
purchase_counts = np.random.poisson(lam=np.where(months_since_signup > 12, 8, 3), size=N)
purchase_counts = purchase_counts.clip(0, 60)

avg_order_values = np.random.lognormal(4.2, 0.7, N).clip(5, 2000).round(2)
# Inject outliers (~1%)
outlier_idx = np.random.choice(N, size=int(N*0.01), replace=False)
avg_order_values[outlier_idx] = np.random.uniform(3000, 15000, len(outlier_idx))

support_tickets = np.random.poisson(1.2, N).clip(0, 20)
review_scores   = np.random.choice([1,2,3,4,5], N, p=[0.08,0.12,0.20,0.35,0.25])

# account_balance with outliers
account_balances = np.random.lognormal(5.5, 1.2, N).clip(0, 10_000).round(2)
bal_outliers = np.random.choice(N, size=int(N*0.005), replace=False)
account_balances[bal_outliers] = np.random.uniform(50_000, 200_000, len(bal_outliers))

# Churn label: high support tickets + low review scores + few purchases → more likely to churn
churn_score = (
    (support_tickets / 10) * 0.30 +
    ((5 - review_scores) / 4) * 0.35 +
    (1 - purchase_counts.clip(0,20) / 20) * 0.25 +
    np.random.uniform(0, 0.1, N)
)
churn_labels = (churn_score > 0.45).astype(int)

# Last purchase date (churned customers have older last purchase)
last_purchase_offsets = np.where(
    churn_labels == 1,
    np.random.randint(180, 730, N),   # churned: 6–24 months ago
    np.random.randint(7,  180, N)     # active:  1 week–6 months ago
)
last_purchase_dates = [
    (end_date - timedelta(days=int(d))).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
    for d in last_purchase_offsets
]

# ── Review text (simple templates) ───────────────────────────
positive_templates = [
    "Great product, fast shipping! Very happy with my purchase.",
    "Excellent quality and arrived on time. Will buy again.",
    "Really satisfied with the customer service. 5 stars.",
    "Good value for money. Product exactly as described.",
    "Fantastic experience from start to finish!",
]
negative_templates = [
    "Terrible customer service. Waited 3 weeks for delivery.",
    "Product broke after one week. Very disappointed.",
    "Not as described. Waste of money.",
    "Horrible experience. Will never shop here again.",
    "Support was useless. Still waiting for my refund.",
]
neutral_templates = [
    "Product is okay. Nothing special.",
    "Delivery was a bit slow but product is fine.",
    "Average quality. Expected better for the price.",
    "It works. Not impressed but not disappointed either.",
]

def get_review(score):
    if score >= 4:
        return random.choice(positive_templates)
    elif score <= 2:
        return random.choice(negative_templates)
    else:
        return random.choice(neutral_templates)

review_texts = [get_review(s) for s in review_scores]

# ── Assemble base DataFrame ───────────────────────────────────
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "customer_id":        [f"CUST{i:06d}" for i in range(1, N+1)],
    "name":               names,
    "email":              emails,
    "age":                ages,
    "income":             incomes,
    "region":             regions,
    "job_title":          job_titles,
    "signup_date":        [d.strftime("%Y-%m-%d") for d in signup_dates],
    "last_purchase_date": last_purchase_dates,
    "purchase_count":     purchase_counts,
    "avg_order_value":    avg_order_values,
    "account_balance":    account_balances,
    "support_tickets":    support_tickets,
    "review_score":       review_scores,
    "review_text":        review_texts,
    "churn":              churn_labels,
})

# ── Inject Missing Values ─────────────────────────────────────
# income: 8% missing (MAR — older customers less likely to report)
income_missing_idx = df[df['age'] > 50].sample(frac=0.16, random_state=1).index
df.loc[income_missing_idx, 'income'] = np.nan
# Additional random missing
df.loc[np.random.choice(df.index, int(N*0.02), replace=False), 'income'] = np.nan

# age: 3% missing
df.loc[np.random.choice(df.index, int(N*0.03), replace=False), 'age'] = np.nan

# job_title: 5% missing
df.loc[np.random.choice(df.index, int(N*0.05), replace=False), 'job_title'] = np.nan

# last_purchase_date: 4% missing (new customers who never purchased)
new_customers = df[df['purchase_count'] == 0].index
df.loc[new_customers, 'last_purchase_date'] = np.nan
df.loc[np.random.choice(df.index, int(N*0.02), replace=False), 'last_purchase_date'] = np.nan

# ── Inject Duplicates (~3%) ───────────────────────────────────
dup_source = df.sample(frac=0.03, random_state=7).copy()
# Slightly vary the duplicates (realistic data entry errors)
dup_source['name'] = dup_source['name'].apply(
    lambda n: n.replace('a','@').replace('e','3') if random.random() < 0.4 else n
)
dup_source['customer_id'] = [f"CUST{i:06d}" for i in range(N+1, N+1+len(dup_source))]
df = pd.concat([df, dup_source], ignore_index=True).sample(frac=1, random_state=99).reset_index(drop=True)

# ── Save ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
df.to_csv('ecommerce_customers.csv', index=False)

print(f"✅ Dataset saved: ecommerce_customers.csv")
print(f"   Rows:          {len(df):,}")
print(f"   Columns:       {df.shape[1]}")
print(f"   Churn rate:    {df['churn'].mean():.1%}")
print(f"   Missing (income): {df['income'].isna().sum():,} ({df['income'].isna().mean():.1%})")
print(f"   Missing (age):    {df['age'].isna().sum():,} ({df['age'].isna().mean():.1%})")
print(f"   Approx duplicates:{len(dup_source):,}")
print(f"   Outlier rows:     ~{len(outlier_idx) + len(bal_outliers):,}")
print("
Column summary:")
print(df.dtypes)
print("
First 3 rows:")
print(df.head(3).to_string())

import pandas as pd
from ydata_profiling import ProfileReport

# Load dataset
df = pd.read_csv('ecommerce_customers.csv')

# Quick overview
print(f"Shape: {df.shape}")
print(f"Missing values:\n{df.isnull().sum()}")
print(f"Duplicates: {df.duplicated().sum()}")

# Automated profiling report
profile = ProfileReport(df, title="Customer Data Quality Report",
                        minimal=True)
profile.to_file("data_quality_report.html")

# Data quality scorecard
quality_issues = pd.DataFrame({
    'Issue': ['Missing Values', 'Duplicates', 'Outliers', 'Format Issues'],
    'Columns Affected': [df.isnull().any().sum(), 1, 3, 2],
    'Records Affected': [df.isnull().sum().max(), df.duplicated().sum(), 
                         245, 1203],
    'Severity': ['High', 'Medium', 'Low', 'Medium']
})
print(quality_issues.to_markdown(index=False))
steps.deliverable: Data quality report HTML file + quality scorecard table + executive summary paragraph
steps.hint: Focus on understanding WHY data is missing (MCAR, MAR, or MNAR) — this determines the best imputation strategy. Check if missing values in 'income' correlate with 'age' or 'occupation'.

steps.codeSnippet:
from sklearn.experimental import enable_iterative_imputer
from sklearn.impute import IterativeImputer, KNNImputer
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestRegressor
import numpy as np

# ML-based imputation for numerical columns
num_imputer = IterativeImputer(
    estimator=RandomForestRegressor(n_estimators=50, random_state=42),
    max_iter=5,
    random_state=42
)

numerical_cols = ['income', 'age', 'account_balance', 'avg_order_value']
df[numerical_cols] = num_imputer.fit_transform(df[numerical_cols])

# KNN imputation for remaining features
knn_imputer = KNNImputer(n_neighbors=5, weights='distance')
df_clean = pd.DataFrame(
    knn_imputer.fit_transform(df),
    columns=df.columns
)

# Validate: compare distributions
from scipy import stats
for col in numerical_cols:
    ks_stat, p_value = stats.ks_2samp(df[col].dropna(), df_clean[col])
    print(f"{col}: KS={ks_stat:.3f}, p={p_value:.3f}")
steps.deliverable: Cleaned dataset CSV + cleaning validation report showing before/after distributions
steps.hint: A p-value > 0.05 in the KS test means the imputed distribution is statistically similar to the original — a good sign. If p < 0.05, your imputation may be distorting the data.

from lightgbm import LGBMClassifier
from sklearn.model_selection import StratifiedKFold, cross_val_score
from imblearn.over_sampling import SMOTE
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score, classification_report
import shap
import optuna

def objective(trial):
    params = {
        'n_estimators': trial.suggest_int('n_estimators', 100, 1000),
        'learning_rate': trial.suggest_float('learning_rate', 0.01, 0.3, log=True),
        'num_leaves': trial.suggest_int('num_leaves', 20, 100),
        'min_child_samples': trial.suggest_int('min_child_samples', 10, 100),
        'subsample': trial.suggest_float('subsample', 0.6, 1.0),
        'colsample_bytree': trial.suggest_float('colsample_bytree', 0.6, 1.0),
        'random_state': 42
    }
    model = LGBMClassifier(**params)
    smote = SMOTE(sampling_strategy=0.3, random_state=42)
    X_res, y_res = smote.fit_resample(X_train, y_train)
    skf = StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, shuffle=True, random_state=42)
    scores = cross_val_score(model, X_res, y_res, cv=skf, scoring='roc_auc')
    return scores.mean()

study = optuna.create_study(direction='maximize')
study.optimize(objective, n_trials=50, show_progress_bar=True)

best_model = LGBMClassifier(**study.best_params)
best_model.fit(X_train_resampled, y_train_resampled)

# SHAP explanations

shap_values = explainer.shap_values(X_test)

steps.hint: If your AUC is above 0.85, you're in good shape. Focus on the business interpretation: what does a 10% improvement in recall mean in terms of customers saved and revenue retained? Always connect model metrics to business value.

steps.codeSnippet:
from transformers import pipeline
from bertopic import BERTopic
import pandas as pd

# Aspect-based sentiment analysis
absa = pipeline("text-classification",
                model="yangheng/deberta-v3-base-absa-v1.1")

aspects = ['product quality', 'shipping speed', 
           'customer service', 'value for money']

def analyze_aspects(review_text):
    results = {}
    for aspect in aspects:
        input_text = f"[CLS] {review_text} [SEP] {aspect} [SEP]"
        result = absa(input_text)[0]
        results[aspect] = {
            'sentiment': result['label'],
            'confidence': result['score']
        }
    return results

# Apply to all reviews
df['aspect_sentiments'] = df['review_text'].apply(analyze_aspects)

# Topic modeling on negative reviews
negative_reviews = df[df['overall_sentiment'] == 'NEGATIVE']['review_text'].tolist()
topic_model = BERTopic(min_topic_size=30, nr_topics=15)
topics, _ = topic_model.fit_transform(negative_reviews)
print(topic_model.get_topic_info().head(10))
steps.deliverable: NLP analysis notebook + aspect sentiment heatmap by customer segment + topic model visualization + correlation analysis between NLP features and churn + automated response templates
steps.hint: The most valuable insight is usually the correlation between sentiment decline and churn. A customer whose review sentiment has been declining for 3+ months is a strong churn signal — even if their most recent review is neutral.
